In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EF problems are age related in children and adolescents with an ASD, and are associated with autism symptom severity.
EF problems in everyday life are not related to age, and that EF problems do not seem to be related to ASD symptom severity.
EF problems are present across the age spectrum, but that there is a shift in which EF problems are more prominent at different ages, and that this shift may be related to ASD symptom severity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the age-related differences in EF problems found in the ASD group were not related to the severity of the ASD symptoms.
EF problems are not a core deficit of autism, but that they are a heterogeneous phenomenon that may vary with age and ASD symptom severity.
EF problems in everyday life in ASD are not only related to age and autism severity, but also to the developmental stage in the life span of the individual. (C) 2015 The Authors. Published
The main takeaway from our work is that
EF problems in ASD are not a uniform construct, but rather a heterogeneous set of problems, that are age-related, and may differ from the EF problems observed using laboratory tasks.
EF problems are present in a substantial proportion of children and adolescents with autism, and that these problems are age dependent.
EF problems in everyday life are present in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorders, with age-related differences in specific EF skills.
